title: The "no writable record" rule lives in three places with different conditions
evidence: Follows S52. ios/HealthRoadmap/MyData/RecordStore.swift:399 (now :400) applyInTurn refuses on predatesErase or (drawn == nil and problem == nil); RecordStore+Uploads.swift:27 and :75 refuse on predatesErase alone; RecordStore+Readable.swift:14 readable is nil on predatesErase or an empty recordJSON. Three readings of one question (may this record be read or written?) that can drift apart. A candidate for one named state on the store, read by all three. US-25 AC16f, AC21 | 2026-11-14: lead S67 names the held state RecordStore.heldUndrawn (RecordStore+Readable.swift), read by redraw and applyInTurn; a natural first piece of S55's one state (held undrawn, predates erase, none loaded, readable), not built here. | done 2026-11-14: one computed state, RecordStore.Hold (RecordStore+Readable.swift: readable, heldUndrawn, empty, unreadable(kept:), predatesErase), read by readable, applyInTurn, the uploads, the charts and redraw; no stored state of its own. Equal to the old conditions on 15 of 16 inputs; the 16th (a drawing with no stored record) cannot occur and now refuses edits, the safe side (owner ruling a). HoldTableTests pins the 16 rows and replaces HeldUndrawnTableTests.
